title: Eval-driven Quality SLO & Error Budget Triage Runbook
author: Morgan Li
content:
Overview

This runbook defines how Redwood SREs and Model Owners operationalize quality SLOs that are driven by recurring evals (acceptance test suites, regression suites and monitoring prompts). It ties eval outputs to an error budget, describes telemetry and alerting, and provides a step-by-step triage and mitigation procedure for quality regressions that impact customers.

Scope

- Applies to any production inference service and model variant that has a defined Quality SLO (examples: /v1/generate text models, embedding models, and rerank endpoints).
- Covers measurement, alerting, incident triage, containment, rollback, and post-incident review for quality regressions (not pure infra outages).

Definitions

- Quality SLO: A service-level objective expressed as the acceptable rate of passing a curated eval test-suite over a rolling window (e.g., 99% pass rate over 28d).
- Eval Job: A scheduled job that runs a deterministic set of prompts/cases against a production model to produce metrics (pass_rate, f1, rouge, latency).
- Error Budget (quality): The complement of the SLO (e.g., SLO=99% -> budget=1% over the SLO window). Burning the budget indicates degraded quality.
- Regression Alert: An automated alert triggered when the rolling pass_rate drops below the alert threshold (usually SLO - delta).

Principles

- Ground SLOs in deterministic evals: production traffic sampling is useful for signal, but SLOs and error budgets are measured from the curated eval harness to be repeatable and auditable.
- Fast containment, slow blame: prioritize rollback/mitigation over root cause attribution.
- Link SLO burn to operational playbooks: burn should trigger staged mitigations (canary rollback, deploy freeze, throttling).

SLO design guidance (recommended defaults)

1) Metric: eval.pass_rate (fraction of eval cases classified as PASS on the golden/acceptance suite).
2) Window: rolling 28-day for contractual SLOs; 7-day for short-lived experimental SLOs.
3) Target: 99.0% for GA models; 99.8% for critical enterprise tenants (customer-specific SLOs live in Dedicated contracts).
4) Alert thresholds:
   - Warning: pass_rate <= SLO - 0.25% (7-day window)
   - Incident: pass_rate <= SLO - 0.75% (24-hour window)
5) Error budget: budget = 1 - SLO (example: 1.0% for 99% SLO). Track burn-rate as budget_used / budget_size over the SLO window.

Example SLO table

| Model | Eval Suite | Window | SLO | Error Budget | Criticality | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| text-clarity-v2 | clarity-acceptance-v1 | 28d | 99.0% | 1.0% | high | @ml-service-steward |
| embed-semantic-v1 | embed-stability-v1 | 7d | 98.5% | 1.5% | medium | @embedding-team |

Telemetry and dashboards

- Eval-runner -> telemetry pipeline produces metrics: eval.pass_rate, eval.mean_f1, eval.case_breakdown[failing_case_id], eval.job_run_duration.
- Dashboards: Quality SLO Overview (per-model, per-tenant), Case Heatmap (failing prompts by tag), Error Budget Burn Chart (28d view).
- Alerting: PagerDuty for Incident alerts (quality-incident), Slack channel #sre-quality for warning alerts.

Alert rules (examples)

1) Incident alert (firing):
   - condition: eval.pass_rate (24h) < SLO - 0.75%
   - severity: P1
   - notify: pd-sre-quality (escalation policy), #sre-quality, model-owner oncall

2) Warning alert (non-pagerduty):
   - condition: eval.pass_rate (7d) < SLO - 0.25%
   - severity: P3
   - notify: #sre-quality, mailbox-model-owners

Runbook: Quality SLO Breach (Incident triage steps)

This section defines a rapid, ordered checklist to contain model-quality incidents. Ownership: the oncall SRE + oncall model steward.

1) Acknowledge and classify (0-10m):
   - Acknowledge PagerDuty alert.
   - Record initial facts in the incident doc: model name, variant, eval suite name, current pass_rate, window and immediate burn rate.

2) Scope and blast radius (10-30m):
   - Check production traffic signals: Is customer-facing error rate or user complaints increasing? (metrics: api.error_rate, api.latency, customer-telemetry).
   - Check tenant-level SLOs (if multi-tenant): identify impacted tenants and their contractual criticality.

3) Triage with eval evidence (15-45m):
   - Open latest eval-job artifact (link from dashboard). Inspect failing_case_ids and clusters.
   - Run the failing eval cases manually against the production endpoint and the previous stable model (if available) to confirm regression. Use the eval harness: 

     $ eval-runner run --suite clarity-acceptance-v1 --model text-clarity-v2 --output /tmp/run-123.json

   - Compare outputs using the eval-compare tool:

     $ eval-compare /tmp/run-123.json /tmp/previous-stable-run.json --report short

4) Containment and mitigation (30-90m): (choose the least disruptive effective action)
   - If regression reproduces and is customer-impacting, prioritize rollback to last known-good model variant.
     - Rollback command (example): 

       $ rctl deploy rollback --service inference-text --model-variant text-clarity-v1 --reason "quality SLO breach"

   - If rollback is not possible or slow, apply policy-driven routing to divert traffic to Dedicated/backup variants: 

       $ rctl routing set --service inference-text --policy "prefer: text-clarity-v1; fallback: text-clarity-v2-readonly"

   - For noisy single-case failures, consider adding short-term case-level patches (score thresholds, prompt fixes) with signoff from model owners. Document these as temporary mitigations.

5) Verify recovery (30-120m):
   - Confirm eval.pass_rate returns above the incident threshold and that customer signals normalize.
   - If rollback occurred, confirm histograms for other metrics (latency, error rate) remain within SLOs.

6) Communicate and runbook closure (within 24h):
   - Post an incident summary to #sre-quality and to the product owner with the initial timeline, actions taken, and immediate impact.
   - If error budget was exhausted or materially reduced for a tenant, partner with Customer Success to coordinate credits/communication per the crediting policy.

Post-incident review and standards

- If incident led to > 25% of error budget consumed in a 28d window OR customer facing impact > P2, perform a formal incident review within 5 business days. Required artifacts: incident timeline, eval artifacts, model diffs, deployment changelog, and mitigation commands executed.
- Use the template: "Incident -> Eval Regression Review" and include a replayable test harness (CI job) that reproduces the failing eval cases.
- Action items must be tracked in the SLO remediation board and assigned to owners with due dates.

Operational tooling and automation suggestions

- Eval-runner: schedule nightly runs (staggered across regions) that push artifacts to object storage and emit metrics to the telemetry pipeline.
- Auto-triage job: on incident alert, create a triage ticket with links to last 3 eval runs, diffs and top N failing cases.
- Rollback safe-guard: require two-step authorization for model rollouts to production (oncall SRE + model steward) with an audit log.

Rollout & canary checklist (pre-deploy)

- Pre-deploy: run the full acceptance suite and a seeded traffic replay against the canary.
- Canary-window: run 24–72h with daily eval checks and 95th percentile of pass_rate >= production SLO.
- Stop-deploy criteria: any single-day drop > 0.5% against SLO or any reproducible customer complaint correlated to the canary.

Appendix A — Alert payload examples

- PagerDuty payload (simplified):

  {
    "title": "Quality SLO breach: text-clarity-v2 (eval.pass_rate=98.1%)",
    "service": "sre-quality",
    "details": "pass_rate 24h=98.1% (SLO=99.0%) — failing cases: [case-42, case-117] — run_id: 2025-02-10T03:12Z"
  }

Appendix B — Example eval job YAML

- eval job spec (example):

  name: clarity-acceptance-v1
  schedule: "0 03 * * *"  # UTC daily at 03:00
  suite: clarity-cases-2024-11
  model: text-clarity-v2
  thresholds:
    pass_rate: 0.99
    mean_f1: 0.90

Appendix C — Ownership and contacts

- Oncall SRE: see PD rotation (team: sre-rotation, channel: #sre-oncall)
- Model Steward: check service OWNERS file under repo infra/services/inference-text/OWNERS
- Customer Success escalation: cs-enterprise@redwood.ai
